description: Pearson correlation between predicted and experimental pIC50 (HeLa48h/dark cohort)

measurements.note: ba_acc 0.0→1.0 lifted but pearson within seed-std

ridge remains credible ceiling on exact-row pearson — BUT this 0.572 was measured on the pic50_margin_sweep cohort (HeLa48h/dark, 702 formulations / 383 scaffolds, seeds 42/0/1234), which is a DIFFERENT split from the wf_pearson_diag / wf_pearson_ridge_gpu diagnostic (joint split, seeds 0/1/2, n_test=994). Treat 0.572 as NOT same-protocol; on the diagnostic's own split the ridge-on-Morgan baseline is 0.3232.

measurements.run: wf124_p3_30epoch_seed0 (Ru multi-task + Wasserstein + L2 guard, GPU-1 RTX 5090)
measurements.note: Ru seed=0 test_pearson (single-seed, 30-epoch multi-task D-MPNN + W₂ pIC50 reg + L2 guard) = 0.3091 — measured on HeLa48h/dark cohort, NOT a HeLa48h cross-cohort. Better than wf_pic50_margin_sweep BEST (0.207) but still below ridge ceiling (0.572). Honest framing: the lift on Ru is real (multi-task + W₂ helps the pIC50 regression side) but ridge remains the credible ceiling. Close-out at TODO/completed/120_m1_ru_auc_strengthen.md and joint TODO/completed/131_m1_m19_joint_rescue.md.

measurements.run: wf131_p1_10epoch_3seed (Ru multi-task + Wasserstein + L2 guard, mean)
measurements.note: Ru × 3-seed × 10-epoch mean test_pearson = 0.260 ± 0.046 (per-seed 0.273 / 0.309 / 0.198). Stable across 3 seeds; better than wf_pic50_margin_sweep BEST (0.207). Same cohort / split as wf124_p3_30epoch_seed0; lower pearson is consistent with shorter training (10 epochs vs 30).

measurements.run: wf_pearson_ridge_gpu (Ru D-MPNN 30-epoch, neural head vs ridge readout on SAME frozen encoder embedding)
measurements.note: DECISIVE head-vs-feature probe on ONE split (Ru, n_train=2262/n_val=394/n_test=994; current MetalCytoToxDB.csv snapshot, NOT the 2026-09 wf124 snapshot). Command: `python molmetal/scripts/train_dmpnn_multitask_wasserstein.py --metals Ru --seeds 0 --epochs 30 --device cuda:0 --no-bf16 --pic50-ridge-readout --csv .data/molmetal/metalcytotox_5metal_multitask_v4.csv --data-csv .data/molmetal/MetalCytoToxDB.csv`. Neural HEAD test_pearson=0.0113; Ridge READOUT on the SAME 2H-dim encoder embedding test_pearson=0.3402 (rmse 0.586 vs head 1.199, ridge_alpha=100). The readout extracts ~30x the signal the neural head extracts. Full report: molmetal/reports/wf_pearson_ridge_gpu/ru/per_seed_metrics_seed0.json.

measurements.run: wf_pearson_diag (alpha-refutation arm, 30-epoch Ru, default vs reg-weighted)
measurements.note: REFUTES the 'regression head is alpha-starved' hypothesis. On the diag split: neural HEAD alpha=0.5 test_pearson=0.2143; neural HEAD alpha=0.2 (reg-weighted) test_pearson=0.1690 (WORSE by -0.045); ridge-on-TRAINED-encoder-embeddings alpha=0.5=0.4074, alpha=0.2=0.3942. Lowering alpha did NOT help the head; a Ridge probe on the same embeddings reaches ~1.9x the head. Ridge-on-Morgan-FP same split=0.3232; ridge-on-RANDOM-encoder-emb=0.3944. Command: `python molmetal/scripts/wf_pearson_r_pic50_head_vs_feature.py --epochs 30 --device cuda:0`. Report: molmetal/reports/wf_pearson_diag/report.json.

wf131_joint_close_out.verdict: MEASURED_PARTIAL_LIFT — Wf-124 P3 Ru seed=0 (30-epoch, multi-task + W₂ + L2 guard) test_pearson = 0.3091 — +0.102 lift over wf_pic50_margin_sweep BEST (0.207), still −0.263 below ridge baseline (0.572). Wf-131 P1 3-seed × 10-epoch mean = 0.260 ± 0.046 (consistent with shorter training). The m1 mechanism lifts both AUC and pIC50 regression; ridge remains the credible ceiling on exact-row pearson.

verdict: MEASURED_HONEST_NEGATIVE + ROOT-CAUSE ISOLATED (2026-10-08) — D-MPNN does not beat ridge on exact-row pearson, AND the bottleneck is the READOUT, not the features or the multi-task alpha. Decisive probe (wf_pearson_ridge_gpu + wf_pearson_diag, one split each): a Ridge probe on the D-MPNN encoder's OWN frozen embedding reaches test_pearson 0.34-0.41, while the neural pIC50 HEAD on the SAME embedding reaches only 0.01-0.21 — the head extracts ~2-30x less signal than a linear probe. Reg-weighting the loss (alpha 0.5 -> 0.2) makes the head WORSE (0.2143 -> 0.1690), refuting the 'head is alpha-starved' hypothesis. Historical best neural 0.3091 (wf124_p3, older 2026-09 split) remains below the ridge ceiling. Honest paper framing: the gap to the historical ridge 0.572 is a readout/architecture problem to be closed with a ridge-or-better readout on the encoder embedding, not a feature problem.
honest_framing: Data source: HeLa48h/dark cohort (Rusanov 2025 phototoxicity subset, exact-row pearson). Model: D-MPNN multi-task + Wasserstein pIC50 reg + L2 guard; ridge regression baseline as ceiling. Protocol: 3-seed × 50-epoch with margin sweep (best margin=0.5). Rusanov 2025 baseline cite-only; iMoLD cite-only. Honest-negative framing per party-twenty-spirit §3.5 (0 容忍 + 不掩盖) — D-MPNN neural (-0.263 below ridge) does not beat ridge on exact-row pearson. Cites TODO-120 (m1 Ru AUC strengthen), TODO-131 (m1+m19 joint rescue), TODO-140/141/142/143/144.

protocol_alignment_2026_10_08.question: Is the historical ridge 0.572 a same-protocol target for our D-MPNN numbers?
protocol_alignment_2026_10_08.verdict: NO — different cohort/split. The 0.572 is from metrics/by_round/pic50_margin_sweep.json (HeLa48h/dark, 702 formulations, 383 scaffolds, seeds 42/0/1234). The 2026-10-08 readout diagnostic runs a joint split with seeds 0/1/2 and n_test=994.
protocol_alignment_2026_10_08.honest_reading: On the diagnostic's own split we already exceed the same-split Morgan ridge (0.4074 vs 0.3232). The 'gap to 0.572' is therefore NOT a same-protocol gap and must not be cited as one. The defensible claim is a READOUT finding: a ridge probe on the frozen encoder embedding extracts ~2x more signal than the neural head.
